sources.title: Google finds attackers running an AI agent that turns security patches into exploits with no human in the loop
sources.summary: Google's threat intelligence team reported an exposed attacker server running "exploit_agent", a multi-agent framework wired to frontier and local models that diffs patched web software, drafts exploits and executes them automatically; victim data from French media and education sites was found on the server. Google says it is the first time it has seen vulnerability discovery and exploitation fully automated by threat actors.

sources.publisher: US Bureau of Industry and Security
sources.title: US issues rule closing remote cloud access to advanced AI chips for China and adding chip licences for five countries
sources.summary: The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule requiring licences for overseas data centres supplying large amounts of advanced AI compute to companies headquartered in China and other embargoed countries, and for advanced chip exports to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. Reporting says the data-centre provisions take effect in 90 days.

sources.title: Google says its multi-agent system autonomously produced a large machine-checked maths formalization
sources.summary: Google Research described /teamwork, a multi-agent feature in Antigravity that runs parallel agents against automated checkers over multi-day tasks. Google says it autonomously produced a roughly 1.8-million-line Lean formalization related to the Weil conjectures and helped on several open problems; the results are self-reported and await independent review.

sources.title: Cursor confirms breach that served a backdoored Claude Code extension to developers
sources.summary: Cursor disclosed that attackers used a key stolen via its AI provider Fireworks to read stored coding-agent traces containing credentials, then served tampered copies of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension from Cursor’s marketplace cache for about 11 hours. Up to 5,000 users may have received the build, which tried to install SSH backdoors.

sources.title: FBI warns attackers are weaponizing an autonomous AI hacking framework
sources.summary: An FBI FLASH alert says multiple threat actors have used the open-source ARTEX agentic penetration-testing framework since August 2026 to automate intrusions across many sectors, in some cases reaching privileged access in under three hours. Named campaigns include theft of personal data on about 67,000 people in South Korea.

sources.title: New York starts registering frontier AI developers under its safety law
sources.summary: New York opened registration for large frontier AI developers under the RAISE Act, run by a new state office (DIGIT) and backed by a new independent evaluation center. From January 2027 covered labs must publish safety frameworks, report critical safety incidents within 72 hours and file regular risk assessments.

sources.title: Espionage group used an AI agent to steal Tajik government documents
sources.summary: CloudSEK reports that an operator linked to the Silent Lynx group ran a self-hosted Hermes agent on DeepSeek to handle reconnaissance, collection and log cleanup, taking more than 2,000 documents from Tajikistan’s government systems. Reuters reported the findings; the attribution is CloudSEK’s.

sources.title: Anthropic reports automated red-team agent breaks its safeguards
sources.summary: Anthropic says Anvil found more and stronger jailbreaks than human red-teamers across biological, cyber, and model-extraction safeguards, and helped improve classifiers. Tests use internal models and classifier visibility, with safeguards disabled on the attacker model; Anthropic says this privileged setup is not currently available to external attackers.

sources.title: OpenAI expands layered monitoring for frontier model misalignment
sources.summary: OpenAI describes layered monitoring for internal frontier agents, reporting measured detection performance on real and synthetic incidents and broader coverage of training, evaluation and tool-using systems. The post also says an independent red-team found several monitoring vulnerabilities, most patched but one still in progress; results are company-reported and not an independent audit of deployment outcomes.

sources.title: OpenAI finds chain-of-thought monitoring can weaken as models scale
sources.summary: OpenAI reports that GPT-6 Astra had lower chain-of-thought monitorability and greater monitor-evasion capability in adversarial tests, while research finds no-CoT reasoning and chain-of-thought controllability rise with training. The company says those measures are imperfect proxies; direct tests of a matched model pair did not show greater evasion for the more controllable model, and Astra did not evade full-context monitoring of complex sabotage without guidance.
